claim: BAY-320 inhibits the recombinant catalytic domain of human Bub1 (amino acids 704–1085) with an IC50 of 680 ± 280 nM in the presence of 2 mM ATP.
source: In presence of 2 mM ATP, both compounds inhibited the recombinant catalytic domain of human Bub1 (amino acids 704–1085) with an IC50 of 680 ± 280 nM and 450 ± 60 nM, respectively (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The IC50 value is derived from in vitro kinase assays measuring inhibition of Bub1 autophosphorylation and histone H2A phosphorylation.

claim: BAY-524 inhibits the recombinant catalytic domain of human Bub1 (amino acids 704–1085) with an IC50 of 450 ± 60 nM in the presence of 2 mM ATP.
source: In presence of 2 mM ATP, both compounds inhibited the recombinant catalytic domain of human Bub1 (amino acids 704–1085) with an IC50 of 680 ± 280 nM and 450 ± 60 nM, respectively (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The IC50 value is derived from in vitro kinase assays measuring inhibition of Bub1 autophosphorylation and histone H2A phosphorylation.

claim: BAY-320 shows only modest cross reactivity with other kinases when tested at 10 μM against a panel of 222 protein kinases.
source: When tested against a panel of 222 protein kinases, BAY-320 showed only modest cross reactivity with other kinases, even when used at a concentration of 10 μM (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Data from a kinase selectivity profiling assay testing BAY-320 against 222 kinases.

claim: BAY-320 shows exquisite binding selectivity for Bub1 when tested against 403 human kinases using an active site-directed competition-binding assay.
source: Furthermore, quantitative measurements of BAY-320 interactions with 403 human kinases, using an active site-directed competition-binding assay, showed exquisite binding selectivity for Bub1 (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Data from a competition-binding assay measuring BAY-320 interactions with 403 human kinases.

claim: Near-maximal inhibition of Bub1 in intact cells can be achieved by using BAY-320 at 3–10 μM.
source: These studies revealed that near-maximal inhibition of Bub1 could be achieved by using BAY-320 at 3–10 μM and BAY-524 at 7–10 μM and these concentrations were therefore used in all future experiments on intact cells.
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence and in-cell western assays monitoring phospho-histone H2A-T120 staining at kinetochores.

claim: Near-maximal inhibition of Bub1 in intact cells can be achieved by using BAY-524 at 7–10 μM.
source: These studies revealed that near-maximal inhibition of Bub1 could be achieved by using BAY-320 at 3–10 μM and BAY-524 at 7–10 μM and these concentrations were therefore used in all future experiments on intact cells.
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence and in-cell western assays monitoring phospho-histone H2A-T120 staining at kinetochores.

claim: Treatment of cells with either BAY-320 or BAY-524 drastically reduces histone H2A T120 phosphorylation.
source: Examination of histone H2A phosphorylation by Western blotting revealed that treatment of cells with either BAY-320 or BAY-524 drastically reduced T120 phosphorylation (Figure 1G).
evidence: Western blot analysis of purified histones from control and inhibitor-treated cells shows reduced T120 phosphorylation.

claim: Depletion of Bub1 from HeLa cells significantly prolongs duration of mitosis due to delayed chromosome alignment and delays in prometa- and metaphase.
source: In line with previous results (Kitajima et al., 2005; Tang et al., 2004b), depletion of Bub1 from HeLa cells significantly prolonged duration of mitosis, due to delayed chromosome alignment and delays in prometa- and metaphase (Figure 2A and C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing mitotic duration in Bub1-depleted HeLa cells, supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Treatment with either BAY-320 or BAY-524 provokes at most minor effects on mitotic progression in HeLa cells, marked by a short delay of anaphase onset.
source: In stark contrast, treatment with either BAY-320 or BAY-524 provoked at most minor effects on mitotic progression, marked by a short delay of anaphase onset (Figure 2B and C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing mitotic duration in BAY-320 or BAY-524 treated HeLa cells.

claim: Diploid RPE1 cells are not significantly affected by either Bub1 inhibition or depletion in terms of mitotic progression.
source: Furthermore, in contrast to aneuploid HeLa cells, diploid RPE1 cells were not significantly affected by either Bub1 inhibition or depletion (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing mitotic duration in RPE1 cells treated with Bub1 inhibitors or depleted of Bub1.

claim: Bub1 depletion causes an increase in the G2/M population of HeLa cells but not RPE1 cells.
source: Flow-cytometric analyses confirmed that Bub1 depletion from HeLa cells causes an increase in the G2/M population of HeLa but not RPE1 cells and that Bub1 inhibition by BAY-320 or BAY-524 did not detectably affect cell cycle profiles in either cell line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: Flow cytometry data showing cell cycle distribution after Bub1 depletion or inhibition.

claim: Bub1 inhibition by BAY-320 or BAY-524 does not detectably affect cell cycle profiles in either HeLa or RPE1 cells.
source: Flow-cytometric analyses confirmed that Bub1 depletion from HeLa cells causes an increase in the G2/M population of HeLa but not RPE1 cells and that Bub1 inhibition by BAY-320 or BAY-524 did not detectably affect cell cycle profiles in either cell line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: Flow cytometry data showing cell cycle distribution after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: Bub1 catalytic activity contributes to the regulation of sister chromatid cohesion.
source: We thus conclude that Bub1 catalytic activity contributes to the regulation of sister chromatid cohesion and the localization of Sgo proteins.
evidence: Chromosome spread analysis showing persistent arm cohesion in cells treated with Bub1 inhibitors.

claim: Bub1 catalytic activity contributes to the localization of Sgo proteins.
source: We thus conclude that Bub1 catalytic activity contributes to the regulation of sister chromatid cohesion and the localization of Sgo proteins.
evidence: Immunofluorescence data showing reduced centromeric levels of Sgo1 and Sgo2 and redistribution of Sgo2 to chromosome arms after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: Centromeric levels of Sgo1 and Sgo2 are reduced to ~20% of control values in BAY-320 or BAY-524 treated cells.
source: Moreover, centromeric levels of Sgo1 and Sgo2 were reduced to ~20% of control values in BAY-320 or BAY-524 treated cells (Figure 3D and E) and, concomitantly, a significant redistribution of Sgo2 to chromosome arms could be observed (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing centromeric Sgo1 and Sgo2 levels after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: A significant redistribution of Sgo2 to chromosome arms occurs in BAY-320 or BAY-524 treated cells.
source: Moreover, centromeric levels of Sgo1 and Sgo2 were reduced to ~20% of control values in BAY-320 or BAY-524 treated cells (Figure 3D and E) and, concomitantly, a significant redistribution of Sgo2 to chromosome arms could be observed (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing Sgo2 levels at centromeres and chromosome arms after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: Bub1 inhibition reduces centromeric levels of Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP by ~50%.
source: While Bub1 inhibition reduced centromeric levels of Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP by ~50% (Figure 4A and B, left panels), depletion of Bub1 lowered centromere levels of these CPC components by ~70% (Figure 4A and B, right panels).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing centromeric levels of CPC components after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: Depletion of Bub1 lowers centromere levels of Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP by ~70%.
source: While Bub1 inhibition reduced centromeric levels of Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP by ~50% (Figure 4A and B, left panels), depletion of Bub1 lowered centromere levels of these CPC components by ~70% (Figure 4A and B, right panels).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing centromeric levels of CPC components after Bub1 depletion.

claim: Both Bub1 inhibition and depletion reduce CENP-A Ser7 phosphorylation by ~50%.
source: Compared to control cells, both Bub1 inhibition and depletion reduced CENP-A and histone H3 phosphorylation by ~50% and ~10–20%, respectively (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that interference with Bub1 primarily affects Aurora B activity at centromeres.
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing CENP-A Ser7 phosphorylation levels after Bub1 inhibition or depletion.

claim: Both Bub1 inhibition and depletion reduce histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation by ~10–20%.
source: Compared to control cells, both Bub1 inhibition and depletion reduced CENP-A and histone H3 phosphorylation by ~50% and ~10–20%, respectively (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that interference with Bub1 primarily affects Aurora B activity at centromeres.
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation levels after Bub1 inhibition or depletion.

claim: Interference with Bub1 primarily affects Aurora B activity at centromeres.
source: Compared to control cells, both Bub1 inhibition and depletion reduced CENP-A and histone H3 phosphorylation by ~50% and ~10–20%, respectively (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that interference with Bub1 primarily affects Aurora B activity at centromeres.
evidence: Differential effects on CENP-A (centromeric) versus histone H3 (chromosome arm) phosphorylation suggest centromere-specific effects.

claim: Both inhibition and depletion of Bub1 reduce the centromere association of the Aurora B effector protein MCAK by ~50%.
source: Furthermore, use of biosensors for Aurora B activity (Fuller et al., 2008) revealed a reduction in fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) ratios for sensors tethered to either chromosome arms (through fusion to H2B) or centromeres (through fusion to histone CENP-B) (Figure 4E and F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing MCAK levels at centromeres after Bub1 inhibition or depletion.

claim: Bub1-dependent phosphorylation plays a major role in the regulation of Aurora B localization and activity.
source: Collectively, these observations demonstrate that Bub1-dependent phosphorylation plays a major role in the regulation of Aurora B localization and activity.
evidence: Multiple lines of evidence including CPC localization, substrate phosphorylation, and FRET-based activity measurements.

claim: Inhibition of Bub1 by BAY-320 or BAY-524 reduces centromere levels of CPC components Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP to ~40%.
source: While inhibition of Bub1 by BAY-320 or BAY-524 or inhibition of Haspin by 5-Iodotubercidin (De Antoni et al., 2012) similarly reduced centromere levels of the CPC components Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP to ~40%, combined inhibition of both kinases resulted in a ~80% reduction in CPC levels at centromeres (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing centromeric CPC levels after Bub1 or Haspin inhibition.

claim: Inhibition of Haspin by 5-Iodotubercidin reduces centromere levels of CPC components Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP to ~40%.
source: While inhibition of Bub1 by BAY-320 or BAY-524 or inhibition of Haspin by 5-Iodotubercidin (De Antoni et al., 2012) similarly reduced centromere levels of the CPC components Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP to ~40%, combined inhibition of both kinases resulted in a ~80% reduction in CPC levels at centromeres (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing centromeric CPC levels after Haspin inhibition, with citation to previous work.

claim: Combined inhibition of both Bub1 and Haspin results in a ~80% reduction in CPC levels at centromeres.
source: While inhibition of Bub1 by BAY-320 or BAY-524 or inhibition of Haspin by 5-Iodotubercidin (De Antoni et al., 2012) similarly reduced centromere levels of the CPC components Aurora B, Borealin and INCENP to ~40%, combined inhibition of both kinases resulted in a ~80% reduction in CPC levels at centromeres (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing centromeric CPC levels after combined Bub1 and Haspin inhibition.

claim: Treatment of cells with only BAY-320 or BAY-524 does not detectably affect the phosphorylation of the Haspin substrate histone H3 (T3).
source: As an important control, treatment of cells with only BAY-320 or BAY-524 did not detectably affect the phosphorylation of the Haspin substrate histone H3 (T3), attesting to the specificity of the two Bub1 inhibitors (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data showing histone H3 T3 phosphorylation levels after Bub1 inhibitor treatment, demonstrating specificity.

claim: Following Bub1 inhibition, Aurora B-EGFP levels at chromosome arms increase approximately twofold.
source: Following Bub1 inhibition, Aurora B-EGFP levels at chromosome arms increased approximately twofold, concomitant with the described reduction of Aurora B at centromeres (Figure 5C and D) (Boyarchuk et al., 2007; Ricke et al., 2012).
evidence: Live cell imaging data of endogenously EGFP-tagged Aurora B showing redistribution to chromosome arms after Bub1 inhibition, with citations to previous studies.

claim: Treatment of cells with the Haspin inhibitor 5-Iodotubercidin does not induce any significant redistribution of Aurora B from centromeres to chromosome arms.
source: In contrast, treatment of cells with the Haspin inhibitor 5-Iodotubercidin did not induce any significant redistribution of Aurora B from centromeres to chromosome arms; instead, inhibition of Haspin caused an overall reduction of EGFP signals at both centromeres and chromosome arms (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Live cell imaging data of endogenously EGFP-tagged Aurora B showing no redistribution after Haspin inhibition.

claim: Inhibition of Haspin causes an overall reduction of Aurora B-EGFP signals at both centromeres and chromosome arms.
source: In contrast, treatment of cells with the Haspin inhibitor 5-Iodotubercidin did not induce any significant redistribution of Aurora B from centromeres to chromosome arms; instead, inhibition of Haspin caused an overall reduction of EGFP signals at both centromeres and chromosome arms (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Live cell imaging data of endogenously EGFP-tagged Aurora B after Haspin inhibition.

claim: Combined inhibition of Bub1 and Haspin displaces Aurora B from both centromeres and chromosome arms.
source: Combined inhibition of Bub1 and Haspin displaced Aurora B from both centromeres and chromosome arms (Figure 5C and D), in line with the analysis of fixed cells described above.
evidence: Live cell imaging data of endogenously EGFP-tagged Aurora B after combined Bub1 and Haspin inhibition.

claim: Bub1 and Haspin cooperate in the recruitment of CPC to centromeres through phosphorylation of histone H2A-T120 and histone H3-T3, respectively.
source: Taken together, these data corroborate the notion that Bub1 and Haspin cooperate in the recruitment of CPC to centromeres through phosphorylation of histone H2A-T120 and histone H3-T3, respectively.
evidence: Multiple lines of evidence showing effects of Bub1 and Haspin inhibition on CPC localization, combined with knowledge of their respective histone substrates.

claim: Bub1 kinase activity, but not Haspin, plays a role in restricting CPC localization to the centromere.
source: In addition, they reveal a role for Bub1 kinase activity, but not Haspin, in restricting CPC localization to the centromere.
evidence: Differential effects of Bub1 versus Haspin inhibition on Aurora B redistribution to chromosome arms.

claim: Depletion of Bub1 weakens SAC signaling in human cells.
source: Depletion of Bub1 is known to weaken SAC signaling in human cells (Klebig et al., 2009; Meraldi and Sorger, 2005; Perera et al., 2007).
evidence: Citations to previous studies demonstrating weakened SAC signaling after Bub1 depletion.

claim: Bub1 inhibition does not significantly affect the localization of Mad1, Mad2, or BubR1 to kinetochores, with the possible exception of a very minor effect on BubR1.
source: With the possible exception of a very minor effect on BubR1, the localization of none of these SAC proteins was significantly affected by Bub1 inhibition (Figure 6A and B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing kinetochore levels of SAC proteins after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: Bub1 depletion decreases kinetochore recruitment of Mad1, Mad2, and BubR1 by 80–90%.
source: In sharp contrast, and in agreement with previous reports (Boyarchuk et al., 2007; Johnson et al., 2004; Overlack et al., 2015; Sharp-Baker and Chen, 2001), Bub1 depletion decreased KT recruitment of all three proteins by 80–90% (Figure 6A and B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing kinetochore levels of SAC proteins after Bub1 depletion, with citations to previous studies.

claim: The recruitment of several SAC components to kinetochores strongly depends on Bub1 protein, but not Bub1 kinase activity.
source: Thus, the recruitment of several SAC components to KTs strongly depends on Bub1 protein, but not Bub1 kinase activity.
evidence: Differential effects of Bub1 inhibition versus depletion on SAC protein recruitment to kinetochores.

claim: Neither BAY-320 nor BAY-524 significantly affects steady-state Bub1 levels at kinetochores.
source: In comparison to control cells, neither BAY-320 nor BAY-524 detectably affected steady-state Bub1 levels at KTs (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B and C), in line with a recent report (Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data showing Bub1 levels at kinetochores after inhibitor treatment, with citation to a recent report.

claim: FRAP experiments reveal only minor effects of Bub1 inhibition on Bub1 dynamics at kinetochores.
source: More importantly, FRAP experiments revealed only minor effects of Bub1 inhibition on Bub1 dynamics at KTs (Figure 6C).
evidence: FRAP data showing Bub1 turnover at kinetochores after inhibitor treatment.

claim: The extent of fluorescence recovery after FRAP of endogenously tagged EGFP-Bub1 is not significantly different in control cells and inhibitor treated cells, revealing an immobile fraction of ~42%.
source: The extent of fluorescence recovery after FRAP was not significantly different in control cells and inhibitor treated cells, revealing an immobile fraction of ~42%, in excellent agreement with previous data (Asghar et al., 2015; Howell et al., 2004).
evidence: FRAP data showing similar recovery plateaus in control and inhibitor-treated cells, with citations to previous studies.

claim: The half-time of Bub1 recovery at kinetochores after FRAP is ~18 sec in control cells.
source: The half-time of Bub1 recovery at KTs after FRAP was ~18 sec in controls, again in good agreement with previous data (Asghar et al., 2015; Howell et al., 2004).
evidence: FRAP data showing Bub1 recovery kinetics in control cells, with citations to previous studies.

claim: Recovery of endogenously tagged wild-type EGFP-Bub1 is only marginally accelerated by Bub1 inhibition (half-time reduced from 18 s to 12–15 s).
source: However, whereas Asghar and colleagues observed a ~50% reduction in the half-time of recovery of an exogenously expressed, catalytically inactive EGFP-Bub1 mutant, we found that recovery of endogenously tagged wild-type EGFP-Bub1 was only marginally accelerated by Bub1 inhibition (half-time reduced from 18 s to 12–15 s) (Figure 6C).
evidence: FRAP data showing Bub1 recovery kinetics after inhibitor treatment, compared to previous study using overexpressed mutant.

claim: The effects of Bub1 activity on Bub1 turnover at kinetochores are at most minor, particularly when compared to the striking effects of Mps1 activity on Mps1 dynamics at kinetochores.
source: We conclude that the effects of Bub1 activity on Bub1 turnover at KTs are at most minor, particularly when compared to the striking effects of Mps1 activity on Mps1 dynamics at KTs (Hewitt et al., 2010; Jelluma et al., 2010; von Schubert et al., 2015).
evidence: FRAP data showing minor effects of Bub1 inhibition on Bub1 dynamics, with citations to studies showing major effects of Mps1 inhibition on Mps1 dynamics.

claim: The percentage of HeLa cells maintaining a SAC arrest over 24 hr drops from 17% in controls to 4% and 2% in response to Bub1 inhibition by BAY-320 and BAY-524, respectively.
source: Over a 24 hr observation period, the percentage of HeLa cells maintaining a SAC arrest dropped from 17% in controls to 4% and 2% in response to Bub1 inhibition by BAY-320 and BAY-524, respectively (Figure 6D, left panel).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing cell fates in nocodazole-arrested HeLa cells after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: In nocodazole-arrested HeLa cells, the percentage of cells undergoing apoptosis increases from 74% in controls to 94% in Bub1-inhibited cells.
source: These shifts in cell fates were largely compensated by increases in the percentages of cells undergoing apoptosis, from 74% in controls to 94% in Bub1-inhibited cells.
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing cell fates in nocodazole-arrested HeLa cells after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: In nocodazole-arrested RPE1 cells, the percentage of arrested cells drops from 61% in controls to 51%/44% in response to Bub1-inhibition.
source: In RPE1 cells, maintenance of SAC arrest over 24 hr was more pronounced, but again the percentage of arrested cells dropped from 61% in controls to 51%/44% in response to Bub1-inhibition, with increasing proportions of cells undergoing apoptosis or mitotic slippage (Figure 6E, left panel).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing cell fates in nocodazole-arrested RPE1 cells after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: Depletion of Bub1 from either HeLa or RPE1 cells results in a 2–3 fold increase in mitotic slippage at the expense of apoptosis.
source: For comparison, depletion of Bub1 from either HeLa or RPE1 cells resulted in a 2–3 fold increase in mitotic slippage at the expense of apoptosis, while the proportion of cells sustaining an arrest remained roughly constant (Figure 6D and E, right panels).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing cell fates in nocodazole-arrested cells after Bub1 depletion.

claim: Bub1 activity contributes to the maintenance of maximal SAC activity, but Bub1 protein levels are more important.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that Bub1 activity contributes to the maintenance of maximal SAC activity, but that Bub1 protein levels are more important, most likely reflecting the observed role of Bub1 in the KT recruitment of SAC components (Figure 6A).
evidence: Comparison of effects of Bub1 inhibition versus depletion on SAC maintenance and SAC protein recruitment.

claim: Bub1 inhibition marginally reduces the time that Reversine-treated cells remain arrested before overriding nocodazole-induced arrest.
source: In agreement with the results described above, Bub1 inhibition marginally reduced the time that Reversine-treated cells remained arrested before overriding nocodazole-induced arrest (Figure 6F and G, left panels).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing duration of mitotic arrest in cells treated with Reversine and Bub1 inhibitors.

claim: Bub1 depletion causes a drastic shortening of mitotic arrest in Reversine-treated cells.
source: Similarly, Bub1 depletion also caused a drastic shortening of arrest (Figure 6F and G, right panels).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing duration of mitotic arrest in cells treated with Reversine after Bub1 depletion.

claim: The scaffolding function of Bub1 is required for the SAC, but its catalytic activity is largely dispensable.
source: Taken together with previous studies (Klebig et al., 2009; Perera and Taylor, 2010a; Perera et al., 2007; Ricke et al., 2012), these observations demonstrate that the scaffolding function of Bub1 is required for the SAC, but its catalytic activity is largely dispensable.
evidence: Comparison of effects of Bub1 inhibition versus depletion on SAC function, combined with citations to previous studies.

claim: Nearly 28% of Bub1-depleted cells fail to completely align all chromosomes after Monastrol washout.
source: While nearly 28% of Bub1-depleted cells failed to completely align all chromosomes, more than 90% of Bub1-inhibited cells showed complete alignment that was indistinguishable from control cells.
evidence: Microscopy data showing chromosome alignment after Monastrol washout in Bub1-depleted cells.

claim: More than 90% of Bub1-inhibited cells show complete chromosome alignment that is indistinguishable from control cells after Monastrol washout.
source: While nearly 28% of Bub1-depleted cells failed to completely align all chromosomes, more than 90% of Bub1-inhibited cells showed complete alignment that was indistinguishable from control cells.
evidence: Microscopy data showing chromosome alignment after Monastrol washout in Bub1-inhibited cells.

claim: Bub1 inhibition only marginally increases the frequency of micronucleation in HeLa and RPE1 cells.
source: While partial inhibition of Aurora B kinase provoked an increase in micronucleation in both cell lines, as expected (Gohard et al., 2014; Tao et al., 2009), Bub1 inhibition only marginally increased the frequency of micronucleation (Figure 7C).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data showing frequency of micronucleation after Bub1 inhibition, with citations to previous studies on Aurora B.

claim: BAY-320 and BAY-524 treatment exerts no significant effects on the kinetochore recruitment of the motor protein CENP-E.
source: Further corroborating this conclusion, we found that BAY-320 or BAY-524 treatment exerted no significant effects on the kinetochore recruitment of the motor protein CENP-E (Figure 7D and E, left panels).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing CENP-E levels at kinetochores after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: Bub1 depletion reduces CENP-E levels at kinetochores by ~40%.
source: In contrast, Bub1 depletion reduced CENP-E levels at KTs by ~40% (Figure 7D and E, right panels), in agreement with previous reports (Johnson et al., 2004; Sharp-Baker and Chen, 2001).
evidence: Quantitative immunofluorescence data showing CENP-E levels at kinetochores after Bub1 depletion, with citations to previous studies.

claim: Bub1 kinase activity is largely dispensable for chromosome congression and segregation.
source: Taken together, these results show that Bub1 kinase activity is largely dispensable for chromosome congression and segregation.
evidence: Multiple lines of evidence including chromosome alignment assays, micronucleation frequency, and CENP-E recruitment.

claim: Even though Bub1 inhibition results in a marked reduction of Aurora B levels at centromeres, these levels are still sufficient to ensure largely faithful chromosome segregation.
source: It follows that even though Bub1 inhibition results in a marked reduction of Aurora B levels at centromeres (Figure 4), these levels are still sufficient to ensure largely faithful chromosome segregation.
evidence: Comparison of Aurora B reduction at centromeres with minimal effects on chromosome segregation fidelity.

claim: Bub1 protein is important for efficient chromosome congression, presumably reflecting the role of Bub1 in CENP-E recruitment to kinetochores.
source: Conversely, Bub1 protein is clearly important for efficient chromosome congression, presumably reflecting the role of Bub1 in CENP-E recruitment to KTs.
evidence: Effects of Bub1 depletion on chromosome alignment and CENP-E recruitment.

claim: Single treatment with 1–4 nM Paclitaxel produces modest impairment of cell proliferation.
source: While single treatment with 1–4 nM Paclitaxel produced modest impairment of cell proliferation, the concomitant application of the Bub1 inhibitors, BAY-320 at 3 μM or BAY-524 at 7 or 10 μM, clearly exacerbated inhibition of proliferation.
evidence: Colony formation assay data showing cell proliferation after Paclitaxel treatment.

claim: Concomitant application of Bub1 inhibitors BAY-320 or BAY-524 with 1–4 nM Paclitaxel clearly exacerbates inhibition of proliferation.
source: While single treatment with 1–4 nM Paclitaxel produced modest impairment of cell proliferation, the concomitant application of the Bub1 inhibitors, BAY-320 at 3 μM or BAY-524 at 7 or 10 μM, clearly exacerbated inhibition of proliferation.
evidence: Colony formation assay data showing cell proliferation after combined Paclitaxel and Bub1 inhibitor treatment.

claim: Effects of combined Paclitaxel and Bub1 inhibitor treatment are particularly drastic in aneuploid HeLa cells.
source: Effects were particularly drastic in aneuploid HeLa cells (Figure 8A and B, top panels), while diploid RPE1 cells were less affected (Figure 8A and B, bottom panels).
evidence: Colony formation assay data comparing effects in HeLa versus RPE1 cells.

claim: Diploid RPE1 cells are less affected by combined Paclitaxel and Bub1 inhibitor treatment compared to aneuploid HeLa cells.
source: Effects were particularly drastic in aneuploid HeLa cells (Figure 8A and B, top panels), while diploid RPE1 cells were less affected (Figure 8A and B, bottom panels).
evidence: Colony formation assay data comparing effects in HeLa versus RPE1 cells.

claim: The combination of Paclitaxel with either Mps1 or Bub1 inhibition produces similar synergistic effects, albeit with cell-type specific differences.
source: This analysis shows that the combination of Paclitaxel with either Mps1 or Bub1 inhibition produced similar synergistic effects, albeit with cell-type specific differences (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: Colony formation assay data comparing effects of Paclitaxel combined with Mps1 or Bub1 inhibition.

claim: Synergy between BAY-320 and Paclitaxel treatment is confirmed for both HeLa and non-small cell lung cancer cells using extensive dose-response analyses.
source: Using extensive dose-response analyses, synergy between BAY-320 and Paclitaxel treatment was further confirmed for both HeLa (Figure 8C) and non-small cell lung cancer cells (Figure 8D).
evidence: IC50 isobologram and combination index analyses showing synergy between BAY-320 and Paclitaxel.

claim: Bub1 inhibition alone does not significantly elevate the frequency of chromosome missegregation in either HeLa or RPE1 cells.
source: Consistent with the micronucleation data described above (Figure 7), Bub1 inhibition alone did not significantly elevate the frequency of chromosome missegregation in either HeLa or RPE1 cells (Figure 8F).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing frequency of chromosome segregation defects after Bub1 inhibition.

claim: HeLa cells display a high frequency of severe chromosome segregation defects when Bub1 inhibition is combined with 1–4 nM Paclitaxel, comparable to the consequences of combined Mps1 inhibition and Paclitaxel treatment.
source: Most importantly, HeLa cells displayed an even higher frequency of severe chromosome segregation defects when Bub1 inhibition was combined with 1–4 nM Paclitaxel, comparable to the consequences of combined Mps1 inhibition and Paclitaxel treatment (Figure 8F).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing frequency of chromosome segregation defects after combined Bub1 inhibition and Paclitaxel treatment.

claim: Bub1 inhibition only marginally elevates the rate of Paclitaxel-induced chromosome missegregation in RPE1 cells.
source: In contrast, Bub1 inhibition only marginally elevated the rate of Paclitaxel-induced chromosome missegregation in RPE1 cells, while combinatorial treatment with Reversine still resulted in a high rate of mild segregation defects.
evidence: Time-lapse imaging data showing frequency of chromosome segregation defects in RPE1 cells after combined Bub1 inhibition and Paclitaxel treatment.

claim: Chromosome segregation errors constitute the most likely cause for the observed impairment of cell proliferation when Bub1 inhibition is combined with low dose Paclitaxel treatment.
source: Considering the strong correlation in the data shown in Figures 7 and 8, it is tempting to conclude that chromosome segregation errors constitute the most likely cause for the observed impairment of cell proliferation when Bub1 inhibition is combined with low dose Paclitaxel treatment.
evidence: Correlation between chromosome segregation defects and impaired proliferation in combined treatment experiments.

claim: Although inhibition of Bub1 kinase activity per se exerts only minor effects on SAC functionality, chromosome segregation and mitotic progression, treatment with BAY-320 or BAY-524 sensitizes cells to low, clinically relevant doses of Paclitaxel.
source: Thus, although inhibition of Bub1 kinase activity per se exerts only minor effects on SAC functionality, chromosome segregation and mitotic progression, treatment with BAY-320 or BAY-524 sensitizes cells to low, clinically relevant doses of Paclitaxel.
evidence: Summary of findings showing minimal effects of Bub1 inhibition alone but synergistic effects with Paclitaxel.

claim: The major conclusion emerging from the present study is that the overall impact of Bub1 inhibition on mitotic progression is surprisingly mild, clearly less severe than the impact of Bub1 depletion.
source: The major conclusion emerging from the present study is that the overall impact of Bub1 inhibition on mitotic progression is surprisingly mild, clearly less severe than the impact of Bub1 depletion.
evidence: Comparison of effects of Bub1 inhibition versus depletion across multiple mitotic processes.

claim: The requirement for Bub1 during chromosome congression and segregation primarily reflects a scaffolding function.
source: This reinforces the notion that the requirement for Bub1 during chromosome congression and segregation primarily reflects a scaffolding function (Fernius and Hardwick, 2007; Klebig et al., 2009; Perera and Taylor, 2010b; Rischitor et al., 2007; Sharp-Baker and Chen, 2001).
evidence: Comparison of effects of Bub1 inhibition versus depletion, combined with citations to previous studies.

claim: Genetic elimination of Bub1 kinase activity is compatible with mouse development.
